The Windowed Fourier Transform (WFT), also known as the Gabor Transform, addresses the lack of spatial localization inherent in the standard Fourier Transform by introducing a spatially localized window function [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the standard Fourier transform is not spatially localized because it covers the whole spatial domain, making it difficult to find the position of irregularities. It then explains that Gabor defined a new decomposition (the windowed Fourier transform) using a spatial window to localize the information. This directly supports the claim that WFT addresses the lack of spatial localization by introducing a window function.
